title: Change summary cards & evidence minimization proposal
body:
Status: very rough PRD sketch (notes + UX ideas). Owner: Dana Kim. Goal: propose a lightweight, operator-focused change summarization UI combined with a privacy-preserving evidence minimization pattern for customer-managed networking and control-plane approval flows.

Why this: customers want concise, machine-readable summaries of operator actions for fast triage and automatic policy decisions (canary/rollback), but they also push back on retention of large packet-level or config diffs for privacy/compliance. Current drafts focus on full evidence bundles or immutable ledgers. This doc explores a middle path: compact summary cards + sampled/derivative evidence + verifiable, compact attestations so we can satisfy audit and rollback needs while minimizing customer-visible PII and storage cost.

High-level idea:
- Every operator-initiated change (network, ACL, rule add/remove, edge-agent upgrade, routing table modify) generates a Change Summary Card (CSC) in the Control Plane UI and API. CSC = short, structured summary (who, when, intent, high-level diff fingerprint, approval path, risk score).
- CSC is the first-class artifact used for UI rollouts, notifications, policy gates and quick forensic triage. Full evidence (config diffs, packet captures, long logs) is captured only when triggered by policy, sampling rules, or manual escalation.
- Compact attestation: the control plane emits a small signed proof (e.g., SHA256 root + operator signature + KMS envelope id) that can be verified by customer SIEM or Redwood support without storing the entire payload. On-demand full evidence retrieval uses a secure, auditable fetch flow (expiration + ephemeral tokens).

Goals and success metrics:
- Reduce average "forensic triage time" by 30% for standard operator errors (measured via case closure time).
- Cut average stored evidence bytes-per-change by >=50% for customers on private deployment default retention.
- Maintain verifiability: support cryptographic chain-of-trust checks for 95% of customer audits (measured by pilot feedback).
- UX: provide at-a-glance rollbacks and policy decisions using CSCs in Console.

Non-goals:
- This doc does not replace long-term immutable archival for high-risk customers who require full packet retention.
- It is not a complete cryptographic design (we'll prototype Merkle-lite approach separately).

User stories:
- Platform operator: "I want to see a concise card that tells me the change intent, affected tenants/edges, and whether the change passed automated approval gates so I can triage a regression quickly."
- Customer security reviewer: "I need a verifiable statement that a change occurred and who approved it, without immediate exposure to full config payloads unless I request it."
- Automation (ops runbooks): "Trigger automated rollback if CSC risk score > threshold and change is younger than 10 minutes."

CSC structure (proposal fields):
- id: short uuid
- timestamp: ISO string
- actor: name + role (operator, system, API key)
- intent: free-text short phrase + optional enum (network-change, rule-rotate, agent-upgrade, key-rotate)
- scope: list of edge ids / tenant ids (compact string list)
- risk_score: 0-100 (derived from approval history + heuristics)
- approval_path: top-level summary (e.g., delegated-admin -> auto-approve)
- evidence_fingerprint: short fingerprint (e.g., SHA256 of canonicalized diff)
- attestation_reference: KMS envelope id / sig metadata
- links: link to fetch full evidence (ephemeral token endpoint)
- ttl_policy: minimal retention hint (e.g., 7d default for sampled evidence)

Notes: CSC stays tiny (~400 bytes). It is stored in the control plane and can be exported to customer SIEMs in near-real-time.

Evidence minimization patterns:
1) Default: only CSC stored for X days (configurable per-customer), full evidence only sampled at N% or when a policy threshold is violated.
2) Triggered capture: on-policy (risk_score > T), or manual escalation by operator / customer, full payload is pulled into secured evidence store with audit chain.
3) On-demand retrieval: signed attestation points to encrypted blob in object store; retrieval requires ephemeral access token which is logged and creates a "retrieval event" CSC.
4) Proof-of-change: Merkle-lite approach where full diff is split into chunks; control plane stores a compact root hash + per-chunk encrypted pointers. Root + operator signature is sufficient to prove a particular diff existed at time T.

Privacy controls (customer-facing):
- Redaction filters: allow customers to define fields considered PII (ip_addresses, user_emails, secrets) and provide redacted versions of evidence when requested.
- Sampling opt-outs: customers can opt their entire org or particular edges into full-capture mode for X time.

UI/Console UX (sketch ideas):
- Change feed in Console: list of CSCs with badges (OK / Warning / Blocked) and quick actions: "Open evidence", "Request full capture", "Rollback (staged)".
- Card expansion shows intent, short diff highlights (top 3 lines), approval summary, and a short "why flagged" rationale from the risk model.
- Rollback button triggers staged-rollback playbook in dedicated deployments: sends a canary revert to affected edges then escalates if failures continue. The CSC links to rollback runbook instance id.

Operator rollback playbook (draft):
- Preconditions: rollback allowed if actor role in allowed_rollback_roles or if change younger than 30m and risk_score > threshold.
- Steps: 1) issue revert change (staged to 2% of edges) 2) monitor health metrics for 5m 3) expand to 20% if healthy 4) fully revert and close CSC/event or mark as "rollback failed" and open incident.
- Observability hooks: trace id included in CSC so console traces correlate with metrics graphs.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- CSCs emitted for all operator-initiated changes in private deployments (control-plane instrumented)
- Console shows change feed and card details (mock data OK)
- API to fetch CSC and to request full evidence (returns ephemeral URL)
- Signed attestation produced per CSC; verification tool in repo (prototype)
- Default retention policy applied with configuration toggle per customer

Telemetry & SLOs:
- Emit metrics: csc_created, csc_fetch_requests, evidence_retrievals, rollback_initiations, rollback_success_rate, bytes_stored_per_change
- SLO: ephemeral evidence retrieval should succeed < 3s in >= 95% of requests for standard sizes (small diffs).

Security / compliance considerations:
- Attestations signed by control-plane KMS key; private deployments should support customer KMS integration (bring-your-key) so attestation chain can use customer-controlled keys.
- Retrieval flow must require both control-plane authorization and ephemeral credential exchange validated against approval path.
- Audit trail must include who fetched evidence and why (reason field required on manual fetch).

Open questions / risks (TODO items):
- How to canonicalize diffs deterministically across edge agents to avoid fingerprint mismatches? (Ethan to prototype canonicalizer)
- Merkle-lite design: chunking strategy and encryption model (Marco + infra)
- Legal/compliance: is a fingerprint+attestation enough for regulators in regulated industries? We need legal signoff.
- UX: how many quick actions do we surface vs. bury behind "more"? (Priya to run 3 quick interviews with SREs)
- Cost model: what is a reasonable default sampling rate that balances cost and forensic usability?

Pilot plan (Q2):
- Identify 2 private-deploy customers willing to trial: one security-conscious large enterprise (full-capture opt-in), one mid-market (sampling default).
- Pilot duration: 6 weeks; collect metrics on triage time, storage delta, and customer feedback.

Next steps (concrete):
- Draft minimal CSC schema in repo (proto/json schema) — owner: Dana (due 2024-02-28)
- Prototype attestation verifier CLI and example using control-plane KMS (Ethan, due 2024-03-08)
- UX quick mockups + interview plan (Priya, due 2024-03-05)
- Infra spike: ephemeral retrieval token flow + expiring pre-signed URL pattern (Marco, due 2024-03-12)

Notes to self: keep CSC intentionally small. Avoid coupling to existing immutable-log work until we have pilot feedback. Capture Slack threads about "attestation" and link them in final PRD.

References and inspiration:
- internal: approval-explainability-and-evidence-summaries-prd-rough (drive)
- external: research notes on "sparse forensics" and "privacy-preserving logging" (attached links in linked_artifacts)

Comments welcome — ping me (dana@redwood.ai) or drop in #private-deployments.

-- end of sketch --
